Question.statement: Which CPU scheduling algorithm achieves the provably minimum average waiting time for a given set of processes arriving simultaneously?
Question.explanation: SJF (non-preemptive when all processes arrive at t=0, or SRTF for varying arrival times) minimizes average waiting time by executing shorter bursts first.

Question.statement: True or False: LRU (Least Recently Used) page replacement suffers from Belady’s Anomaly when the number of physical memory frames is increased.
Question.explanation: LRU is a stack algorithm, meaning the set of pages in memory with n frames is always a subset of pages with n+1 frames. Only non-stack algorithms like FIFO suffer from Belady’s Anomaly.

Question.statement: What are the four Coffman conditions that must hold simultaneously for a deadlock to occur? State the condition broken by ordering resource acquisitions.
Question.correctAnswer: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait; ordering breaks Circular Wait.
rubricPoints: Lists all 4 Coffman conditions accurately (3 marks)
Identifies Circular Wait as broken by total ordering (2 marks)
Question.explanation: Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, and Circular Wait. Assigning a strict global numbering to resource types and requiring increasing acquisition order prevents circular wait.

Question.statement: A relation R is in BCNF if and only if for every non-trivial functional dependency X -> Y holding in R:
options: X is a superkey of R
X is a candidate key only
Y is transitively dependent on X
Question.correctAnswer: X is a superkey of R
Question.explanation: By definition, Boyce-Codd Normal Form requires that the determinant X of every non-trivial FD X -> Y must be a superkey of the relation.

Question.statement: True or False: Every conflict-serializable schedule is guaranteed to be view-serializable, though the converse is not true.
Question.explanation: Conflict serializability is a strictly stronger condition than view serializability. Schedules with blind writes can be view-serializable without being conflict-serializable.

Question.statement: Explain the structural difference between a B-Tree and a B+ Tree index, and describe why B+ Trees are preferred for database range queries.
rubricPoints: Data pointers only at leaf nodes in B+ Tree vs all nodes in B-Tree (3 marks)
Higher fan-out & lower tree height for B+ Tree (3 marks)
Doubly-linked leaf nodes enabling fast sequential range scans (4 marks)
Question.explanation: B+ Trees store record pointers exclusively at leaf level and link leaf nodes sequentially, allowing higher branching factor in internal nodes and O(log n + k) range traversal.

Question.statement: Which class of formal languages is strictly accepted by a Deterministic Pushdown Automaton (DPDA) versus a Non-deterministic PDA?
options: Both accept exactly the same Context-Free Languages
DPDA accepts Deterministic CFLs, a proper subset of CFLs
Question.correctAnswer: DPDA accepts Deterministic CFLs, a proper subset of CFLs
Question.explanation: Unlike finite automata (where DFA = NFA), DPDA is strictly weaker than NPDA. For example, L = { ww^R } requires non-determinism.

Question.statement: True or False: Every Context-Free Grammar without epsilon productions can be converted into Chomsky Normal Form (CNF).
Question.explanation: Any CFG generating a language without the empty string can be systematically transformed into CNF (A -> BC or A -> a) by eliminating unit productions and factoring long RHS.

Question.statement: What is the worst-case time complexity of solving Longest Common Subsequence (LCS) for strings of length m and n using dynamic programming?
Question.explanation: The DP table has (m+1) x (n+1) entries, each computed in O(1) time.

Solution.title: Banker’s Algorithm Safety Sequence & Need Matrix Derivation

steps.heading: Compute the Need Matrix
steps.content: For each process Pi and resource Rj, compute Need[i][j] = Max[i][j] - Allocation[i][j].

steps.heading: Initialize Work and Finish Vectors
steps.content: Set Work = Available vector and Finish[i] = false for all i = 0..n-1.

steps.heading: Find Executable Process
steps.content: Select Pi where Finish[i] == false and Need[i] <= Work. Update Work = Work + Allocation[i] and Finish[i] = true.

steps.heading: Verify Safe Sequence
steps.content: Since all processes finish cleanly in sequence <P1, P3, P4, P0, P2>, the system is in a safe state.

Solution.finalAnswerSummary: Safe sequence exists: <P1, P3, P4, P0, P2>. Additional request for P1 can be granted immediately.

Solution.title: Lossless & Dependency-Preserving BCNF Decomposition

steps.heading: Find Candidate Keys
steps.content: Compute attribute closures from the given FD set F = {AB -> C, C -> D, D -> A}. Candidate keys are AB, BC, BD.

steps.heading: Identify BCNF Violations
steps.content: Check each FD X -> Y. C -> D violates BCNF because C is not a superkey.

steps.heading: Decompose Iteratively
steps.content: Split R into R1(C, D) and R2(A, B, C). Verify lossless join via common attribute C being key of R1.

Solution.finalAnswerSummary: Decomposed tables R1(C,D), R2(D,A), R3(A,B,C) satisfy BCNF with lossless join.

Solution.title: CFG to Chomsky Normal Form (CNF) Transformation

steps.heading: Eliminate Null & Unit Productions
steps.content: Remove nullable symbols and unit rules A -> B cleanly.

steps.heading: Introduce New Non-Terminals
steps.content: Replace terminals inside rules of length >= 2 and split chains into binary rules.
